name: crypto_sha256
description: Computes the SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the input string. SHA-256 is part of the SHA-2 family and produces a 256-bit (32-byte) hash value. Commonly used for data integrity verification and anonymization.

examples.description: Basic usage
examples.code: SELECT crypto_sha256('Hello, World!') AS hash;

examples.description: Anonymize email addresses for analytics
examples.code:
SELECT
  crypto_sha256(email) AS user_id,
  COUNT(*) AS purchases
FROM orders
GROUP BY crypto_sha256(email)
ORDER BY purchases DESC
LIMIT 10;

returns: 64-character hexadecimal string representing the SHA-256 hash

name: crypto_sha512
description: Computes the SHA-512 cryptographic hash of the input. More secure than SHA-256 with a 512-bit output. Recommended for high-security applications.

examples.description: Hash sensitive data with SHA-512
examples.code: SELECT crypto_sha512('sensitive data') AS hash;

returns: 128-character hexadecimal string representing the SHA-512 hash

name: crypto_hash_combine
description: Combines multiple values into a single cryptographic hash. Accepts any number of arguments, concatenates them in order, and produces a SHA-256 hash. Useful for creating composite keys, fingerprinting multiple columns, or generating deterministic IDs from multiple fields.

examples.description: Combine multiple fields into a single hash
examples.code:
SELECT crypto_hash_combine(first_name, last_name, email) AS user_fingerprint
FROM users;

examples.description: Create a composite key from order details
examples.code:
SELECT crypto_hash_combine(
  customer_id::VARCHAR,
  order_date::VARCHAR,
  product_id::VARCHAR,
  quantity::VARCHAR
) AS order_key
FROM orders;

examples.description: Hash a single value (equivalent to crypto_sha256)
examples.code: SELECT crypto_hash_combine('single value') AS hash;

examples.description: Combine many fields for deduplication

returns: 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 hash of all combined values

name: crypto_hmac_sha256
description: Creates an HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) signature using SHA-256. Used for API authentication, webhook verification, and message integrity.

examples.description: Sign API requests with HMAC
examples.code:
SELECT
  request_id,
  payload,
  crypto_hmac_sha256(payload, 'my_secret_key') AS signature
FROM api_requests;

name: crypto_bcrypt
description: Hashes a password using the bcrypt algorithm with automatic salt generation. Recommended for password storage. The cost parameter controls computational cost (2^cost iterations).

examples.description: Hash password with default cost (10)
examples.code:
INSERT INTO users (username, password_hash)
VALUES ('alice', crypto_bcrypt('secret_password'));

examples.description: Hash with custom cost for higher security
examples.code:
INSERT INTO admin_users (username, password_hash)
VALUES ('admin', crypto_bcrypt('admin_password', cost := 12));

examples.description: Explicit named parameter syntax
examples.code: SELECT crypto_bcrypt('my_password', cost := 14) AS secure_hash;

returns: Bcrypt hash string containing salt and hash (60 characters)

name: crypto_bcrypt_verify
description: Verifies a plaintext password against a bcrypt hash. Timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks.

examples.description: Verify user login credentials
examples.code:
SELECT
  user_id,
  username,
  crypto_bcrypt_verify('user_input', password_hash) AS is_valid
FROM users
WHERE username = 'alice';

returns: TRUE if password matches hash, FALSE otherwise

name: crypto_generate_keys
description: Generates RSA public/private key pairs in bulk. Useful for provisioning multiple users or services with cryptographic keys. Returns a table where each row contains one complete key pair.

examples.description: Generate 10 RSA key pairs with default 2048-bit keys
examples.code: SELECT * FROM crypto_generate_keys(10) LIMIT 3;

examples.description: Generate 5 high-security 4096-bit key pairs
examples.code: SELECT * FROM crypto_generate_keys(5, key_size := 4096);

examples.description: Store generated keys in a table
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE user_keys AS
SELECT
  key_id,
  public_key,
  private_key,
  created_at
FROM crypto_generate_keys(100);

examples.description: Generate keys and immediately assign to users
examples.code:
INSERT INTO user_keypairs (user_id, public_key, private_key)
SELECT
  u.user_id,
  k.public_key,
  k.private_key
FROM users u
CROSS JOIN LATERAL crypto_generate_keys(1) k
WHERE u.needs_keypair = true;

returnsTable.name: key_id
returnsTable.description: Unique identifier for the key pair

name: crypto_audit_trail
description: Creates a cryptographic audit trail for database operations using blockchain-style hash chaining. Each record contains a hash of its data plus the previous record's hash, making tampering detectable.

examples.description: Generate audit trail for financial transactions
examples.code: SELECT * FROM crypto_audit_trail('financial_transactions', 'INSERT') LIMIT 5;

examples.description: Verify audit chain integrity and detect tampering
examples.code:
WITH audit AS (
  SELECT * FROM crypto_audit_trail('sensitive_data', 'UPDATE')
)
SELECT
  sequence_num,
  record_hash,
  chain_valid,
  CASE
    WHEN NOT chain_valid THEN 'TAMPERING DETECTED!'
    ELSE 'Valid'
  END AS status
FROM audit
WHERE NOT chain_valid;

returnsTable.name: record_hash
returnsTable.description: SHA-256 hash of the current record

returnsTable.name: chain_valid
returnsTable.description: Whether the audit chain is valid

name: crypto_hash_agg
description: Aggregates multiple values into a single cryptographic hash. Order-independent - produces the same hash regardless of row order. Useful for creating fingerprints of entire datasets or groups.

examples.description: Generate fingerprint for all users
examples.code:
SELECT crypto_hash_agg(email) AS users_fingerprint
FROM users;

examples.description: Hash all transaction IDs for a daily batch
examples.code:
SELECT
  DATE(created_at) AS batch_date,
  crypto_hash_agg(transaction_id) AS batch_hash
FROM transactions
GROUP BY DATE(created_at);

examples.description: Use SHA-512 for higher security
examples.code:
SELECT crypto_hash_agg(sensitive_field, algorithm := 'sha512') AS secure_hash
FROM sensitive_table;

examples.description: Detect data changes by comparing hashes
examples.code:
WITH current_hash AS (
  SELECT crypto_hash_agg(data_column) AS hash FROM production_table
),
backup_hash AS (
  SELECT crypto_hash_agg(data_column) AS hash FROM backup_table
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN c.hash = b.hash THEN 'Data matches'
    ELSE 'Data has changed!'
  END AS status
FROM current_hash c, backup_hash b;

returns: Aggregated hash combining all input values

name: crypto_merkle_root
description: Computes a Merkle tree root hash for a set of values. Like blockchain transaction verification - any change to input data produces a different root. More efficient than concatenating all values for large datasets.

examples.description: Calculate Merkle root for a block of transactions
examples.code:
SELECT
  block_id,
  crypto_merkle_root(transaction_hash) AS merkle_root
FROM blockchain_transactions
GROUP BY block_id;

examples.description: Verify data integrity using Merkle root
examples.code:
WITH daily_blocks AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(timestamp) AS date,
    crypto_merkle_root(record_id::VARCHAR) AS merkle_root
  FROM audit_log
  GROUP BY DATE(timestamp)
)
SELECT
  date,
  merkle_root,
  LAG(merkle_root) OVER (ORDER BY date) AS previous_root
FROM daily_blocks;

examples.description: Create tamper-evident file manifest

name: COPY_ENCRYPTED_PARQUET
description: Exports query results to an encrypted Parquet file with client-side encryption. The entire file is encrypted at rest using AES-256, ensuring data confidentiality during storage and transit. Compatible with standard Parquet readers when decryption keys are provided.

examples.description: Export encrypted user data to Parquet
Export with custom row group size for large datasets
examples.code:
COPY (
  SELECT transaction_id, amount, timestamp, customer_id
  FROM transactions
  WHERE amount > 1000
)
TO 's3://my-bucket/encrypted-transactions.parquet'
WITH (
  ENCRYPTION_KEY 'YourBase64EncodedKey==',
  ROW_GROUP_SIZE 500000,
  COMPRESSION 'SNAPPY'
);

options.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
options.description: Base64-encoded AES-256 encryption key for client-side encryption

options.name: ROW_GROUP_SIZE
options.description: Number of rows per Parquet row group

name: COPY_ENCRYPTED_CSV
description: Exports query results to an encrypted CSV file. The CSV file is encrypted before being written to disk, protecting sensitive data in a portable text format. Useful for secure data exchange with systems that require CSV input.

examples.description: Export encrypted customer data to CSV
examples.code:
COPY (
  SELECT customer_id, name, email, phone
  FROM customers
  WHERE region = 'US'
)
TO 'encrypted_customers.csv'
WITH (
  ENCRYPTION_KEY 'YourSecureKey123',
  HEADER true,
  DELIMITER ','
);

options.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
options.description: Encryption key for securing the CSV file contents

options.name: HEADER
options.description: Include column headers in the output

name: COPY_SIGNED_JSON
description: Exports query results to a cryptographically signed JSON file. Each record is signed with HMAC-SHA256, enabling tamper detection and data integrity verification. The signature is included in the output, allowing consumers to verify authenticity.

examples.description: Export signed API response data
examples.code:
COPY (
  SELECT api_key, rate_limit, created_at, permissions
  FROM api_keys
  WHERE status = 'active'
)
TO 'signed_api_keys.json'
WITH (
  SIGNING_KEY 'your-hmac-secret-key',
  FORMAT 'ARRAY',
  PRETTY true
);

examples.description: Export newline-delimited signed events

options.name: SIGNING_KEY
options.description: HMAC signing key for generating digital signatures

options.name: PRETTY
options.description: Pretty-print the JSON output with indentation
